issues.item: Fear of Rage: I will not be able to control my anger and will do something terrible
issues.explanation: The appraisal of feared uncontrollable rage is not well supported by the rest of the profile. There are no corresponding trigger, threat, memory, or strategy items suggesting anger-driven reactivity, aggression risk, or conflict; the other appraisals instead center on shame and hopelessness after rape. This makes the rage item clinically discordant within the selected five components.

issues.item: Constant Socialising: I keep myself constantly surrounded by people so I am never alone with my thoughts
issues.explanation: The strategy of constant socialising is hard to reconcile with the rest of the profile in this rape-related presentation. The selected triggers are solitary/sensory reminders (silence, outdoor smells, anniversary), and the appraisals are shame, suicidality, and feared rage. Constantly surrounding oneself with people does not connect clearly to these reminders and is somewhat at odds with body shame after rape, making it the least coherent avoidance/coping item here.

vignette: Akua had always found solace in the rhythms of nature. As an agricultural worker on a rural farm, she spent her days tending to the land, nurturing life from the earth. But since that night 10 years ago, when she was brutally raped by a fellow farmhand, the very scents and sounds that once brought her peace now stirred up anguish. The smell of damp soil or fresh-cut grass would transport Akua back to the scene of the attack, where she was pinned down in the dirt. On anniversaries of the event, Akua's mind would become a jumble of memories, each one more searing than the last. And when sudden silence fell over the farm - perhaps during a lull in the wind or after a bird had stopped singing - Akua's heart would skip a beat, as if she was waiting for the sound of footsteps approaching. In an effort to stave off these memories, Akua began to avoid certain circumstances that reminded her of the event. She shunned working in the dark, opting instead for early morning or late afternoon shifts when the sun was high. She also started avoiding physical contact with others, unable to bear the thought of being touched without consent again. Even her partner's gentle caresses felt suffocating at times. Akua had come to believe that her body was tainted by what had happened - that she was somehow dirty or contaminated. This sense of shame and self-loathing seeped into every aspect of her life, making it hard for her to find joy in the simple things. Some days, Akua wondered if her life was worth living anymore; the pain seemed too much to bear. To cope with these dark thoughts, Akua forced herself to think only positive thoughts. She would recite affirmations under her breath, trying to drown out the self-doubt that crept in whenever she was alone. But this strategy had an unintended consequence: it made Akua more attuned to potential triggers. Whenever she caught a whiff of soil or heard an unexpected silence, her mind would immediately start racing with catastrophic thoughts - "I'm not safe," "I'll never be clean again." As the years went by, Akua's avoidance behaviors became more entrenched. She began to withdraw from social gatherings and community events, fearing that someone might touch her or make a comment that would trigger a flashback. Her partner grew concerned about Akua's increasing isolation, but she couldn't explain why it felt like such a threat - only that the thought of being around others made her feel like she was walking on eggshells. Akua's negative appraisals of herself and the world had created a self-reinforcing cycle. The more she avoided certain situations or thoughts, the more convinced she became that they were indeed threats to her safety and well-being. And yet, it was this very avoidance that kept her trapped in a state of hypervigilance, waiting for the next shoe to drop. It wasn't until Akua's partner sat down with her, gently coaxing out the stories she had been keeping hidden, that she began to realize just how stuck she was. The weight of her secrets and the toll they were taking on her relationship finally brought Akua to seek help - not because she hoped for a miracle cure, but because she couldn't bear the thought of living in this state of perpetual fear any longer.
